sectors.note:
**TL;DR:** Technology and Industrials anchor US sector strength as dominant all-green leaders, while Financials show positive momentum rotation despite a low YTD rank.

Market leadership remains highly concentrated, with only 3 of 11 sectors achieving "all-green" status across all timeframes. Technology (momentum 0.93) and Industrials (momentum 0.77) continue to lead the market as the only two sustained strong performers over the 1-, 3-, and 6-month horizons. Financials (momentum 0.59) are showing signs of positive rotation, gaining one spot to rank 8 and joining the all-green list.

Conversely, defensive and cyclical laggards are fading. Consumer Cyclical (momentum 0.20) sits at the bottom of the table at rank 11, while Communication Services (momentum 0.23) and Energy (momentum 0.50) both slipped one spot over the last five sessions. 

## Strength
* **All-Green Breadth:** Only 3 of 11 sectors—Technology (0.93 momentum), Industrials (0.77 momentum), and Financials (0.59 momentum)—are positive across the week, month, quarter, half, and YTD.
* **Sustained Leadership:** Technology and Industrials remain the top two sustained performers across 1-, 3-, and 6-month horizons.
* **Dominant Momentum:** Technology leads all sectors with a momentum score of 0.929, maintaining its #1 YTD rank.

## Movers & Momentum
* **Financials Rotating Up:** Financials improved by +1 spot over the last 5 sessions to rank 8, supported by a solid momentum score of 0.586.
* **Tech Extends Lead:** Technology also gained +1 spot over the last 5 sessions to secure the #1 rank with momentum at 0.929.
* **Decliners:** Energy (momentum 0.50, rank 2) and Communication Services (momentum 0.23, rank 9) both dropped -1 spot over the past 5 sessions.
* **Momentum Laggards:** Consumer Cyclical remains the weakest sector with a momentum score of 0.200 (rank 11), followed closely by Communication Services at 0.229.

## Divergences
* **Financials Momentum vs. Rank:** Financials exhibit strong momentum (0.586) and "all-green" status, yet still sit at a low YTD rank of 8, indicating a potential catch-up trade.
* **Consumer Defensive Decay:** Consumer Defensive holds a moderate YTD rank of 6, but its momentum has deteriorated to a weak 0.257.
* **Energy Slipping:** Despite holding the #2 YTD rank, Energy lost 1 spot this week, with its momentum cooling to a neutral 0.500.
* **No Fragile All-Green:** No sectors currently trigger the fragile all-green early-warning signal, indicating stability among the current top-tier leaders.

industries.note:
**TL;DR:** Tech hardware and industrial infrastructure maintain absolute dominance, while high-beta cyclicals like Airlines, Biotech, and Uranium surge, contrasting with sharp declines in coal and defensive retail.

The market's core strength remains heavily concentrated in hardware, semiconductor equipment, and electrical infrastructure. Computer Hardware (momentum 0.99) and Semiconductor Equipment & Materials (momentum 0.98) continue to lead the 31 "all-green" industry groups, showing sustained dominance across all timeframes. 

A powerful rotation is underway as Airlines, Biotechnology, and Uranium each jumped 23 spots over the last five sessions, signaling a sharp risk-on shift. Conversely, traditional defensives and energy plays are fading rapidly; Coking Coal plummeted 33 spots, Grocery Stores dropped 30 spots into near-bottom momentum territory (0.12), and Staffing & Employment Services fell 23 spots.

## Strength
* **Broad-Based Strength:** 31 out of 144 industry groups are currently "all-green," indicating positive performance across weekly, monthly, quarterly, half-year, and year-to-date horizons.
* **Secular Tech & Infrastructure Leaders:** Computer Hardware (0.99 momentum), Semiconductor Equipment & Materials (0.98), and Electrical Equipment & Parts (0.98) represent the absolute top tier of sustained strength.
* **Heavy Industry Alignment:** Farm & Heavy Construction Machinery (0.94 momentum), Engineering & Construction (0.91), and Semiconductors (0.90) are firmly entrenched in the top 36 sustained lists.

## Movers & Momentum
* **Top Gainers:** Airlines (+23 spots, rank 62, momentum 0.79), Biotechnology (+23 spots, rank 68, momentum 0.72), and Uranium (+23 spots, rank 52, momentum 0.62) led the weekly advance.
* **Severe De-ratings:** Coking Coal fell 33 spots to rank 103 (momentum 0.35), while Grocery Stores plunged 30 spots to rank 114, joining the momentum laggards list with a weak score of 0.12.
* **Momentum Extremes:** Computer Hardware (0.987) and Semiconductor Equipment & Materials (0.984) lead the market YTD, whereas Consulting Services (0.062) and Software - Application (0.094) remain deeply depressed.

## Divergences
* **Fading Momentum:** Several high-momentum groups are beginning to lose rank, notably Steel (momentum 0.70, rank -9), Trucking (momentum 0.68, rank -6), and Department Stores (momentum 0.64, rank -5).
* **Emerging Turnarounds:** Low-momentum groups showing sudden rank improvements include Airports & Air Services (rank +13, momentum 0.38), Gold (rank +11, momentum 0.41), and Real Estate - Diversified (rank +10, momentum 0.44).
